g.text: MANUAL STEPS -- THE WHOLE GITOPS FLOW BY HAND (docs/manual-steps.md)
Read the cards 1 -> 16 (snake). Each card: what you type (terminal), what you see (UI), what it proves (result).
run it yourself: build, test, Helm
= the file / command that does this step for you (docs/automation-steps.md)
- one repo = 3 apps + 1 Helm chart + every environment
- nothing to install yet, just read
RESULT: You know where everything lives.
- kind = Kubernetes inside one Docker container
- the same cluster type the e2e test uses in CI
- CI runs these only for apps that changed
$ sh -c "pip install -q -r requirements-dev.txt && ruff check . && pytest -v"
- CI builds once, for amd64 + arm64
$ for app in orders-api inventory-svc web-frontend; do
Scan the image and the repo
- Trivy: fail only on CRITICAL CVEs that have a fix
- Gitleaks: secrets anywhere in the git history
- same command = same gate as CI
RESULT: 0 CRITICAL vulnerabilities, no leaked secrets.
Render and validate the Helm chart
- one chart for all apps; env files override only differences
- helm template = exactly what the cluster gets
- diff qa vs prod before promoting
RESULT: Chart is valid and you can read prod's YAML.
- namespace hands-on has no GitOps protection
$ for app in orders-api inventory-svc web-frontend; do
Release "orders-api" has been installed. Happy Helming!
- the page shows which version runs here
- the value is never printed, only 'configured: true'
- by hand = kubectl; in GitOps = External Secrets
- never put secrets in values files (git history!)
$ kubectl -n hands-on create secret generic orders-api-secrets \
Upgrade and roll back with Helm
- it works, but who changed it and why? not recorded
- the rollback depends on Helm history inside the cluster
- next steps: make Git the history instead
$ helm upgrade orders-api charts/app -n hands-on --reuse-values --set image.tag=0.1.1
Rollback was a success! Happy Helming!
RESULT: Back on 0.1.0 -- but nothing in Git says why.
Install ArgoCD, hand over to Git
- the ONLY manifest you ever apply by hand
- ArgoCD installs platform + 9 apps from Git
RESULT: 14 applications, all Synced and Healthy.
- deploying = editing one file + git push
- no kubectl apply, no cluster credentials
- ArgoCD picks it up within ~1 minute
$ git commit -am "chore(dev): deploy orders-api 0.1.0" && git push
RESULT: dev runs 0.1.0, and Git records who, when and why.
- copies qa's exact tag + digest, never rebuilds
- a PR = review + audit trail for prod
- roll back = git revert the merge commit
$ git switch -c promote/orders-api && git commit -am "chore(prod): promote orders-api"
All checks have passed (CI/CD, Security, PR title)
RESULT: Merged: prod runs the same bytes qa tested.
- even cluster-admin is blocked in demo-* namespaces
- only ArgoCD's controller may change workloads
- stops kubectl / Rancher drift that self-heal misses
$ kubectl -n demo-prod set image deploy/orders-api orders-api=nginx:1.29
error: failed to patch image update to pod template:
Manual changes are blocked in GitOps namespaces
(you are kubernetes-admin). Change the files in Git instead -
RESULT: DENIED -- that is the point. Git is the only way in.
- GitOps Delivery: sync, health, version per env
- every alert links to a runbook in docs/runbooks
RESULT: You see what runs where, and how often you deploy.
- make up rebuilds it from Git in minutes
- that is the point of GitOps
RESULT: Laptop clean. Run make up to get it all back.
